formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (AB : Line) (C : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) ∧ (¬(a.onLine C)) ∧ (|(a─b)| > |(c─a)|)) → (∃ e : Point, e.onLine AB ∧ |(a─e)| = |(c─a)|)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c : Point) (AB : Line) (C : Line) (h1 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) (h2 : ¬(a.onLine C)) (h3 : |(a─b)| > |(c─a)|) : ∃ e : Point, e.onLine AB ∧ |(a─e)| = |(c─a)| := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (AB : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) ∧ (|(a─b)| ≠ |(a─c)|)) → (∃ ae : Point, (|(a─ae)| = |(a─c)|) ∧ between a ae b)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c : Point) (AB : Line) (h1 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) (h2 : |(a─b)| ≠ |(a─c)|) : ∃ ae : Point, (|(a─ae)| = |(a─c)|) ∧ between a ae b := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (AB : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) ∧ (¬(c.onLine AB))) → (exists h : Point, h.onLine AB ∧ ((∠ a:h:c : ℝ) = ∟ ∨ (∠ b:h:c : ℝ) = ∟))
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c : Point) (AB : Line) (h1 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) (h2 : ¬(c.onLine AB)) : exists h : Point, h.onLine AB ∧ ((∠ a:h:c : ℝ) = ∟ ∨ (∠ b:h:c : ℝ) = ∟) := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (AB : Line) (C_line : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) ∧ (c ≠ a) ∧ (¬(c.onLine AB)) ∧ (|(a─c)| < |(a─b)|)) → (∃ e : Point, (e.onLine AB ∧ |(a─e)| = |(a─c)|))
formalizations.full_output: theorem theorem_unequal_straight_lines (a b c : Point) (AB C_line : Line) (h1 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) (h2 : c ≠ a) (h3 : ¬(c.onLine AB)) (h4 : |(a─c)| < |(a─b)|) : ∃ e : Point, (e.onLine AB ∧ |(a─e)| = |(a─c)|) := by

reference_formalization: ∀ (a b c₀ c₁ : Point) (AB C : Line), distinctPointsOnLine a b AB ∧ distinctPointsOnLine c₀ c₁ C ∧ |(a─b)| > |(c₀─c₁)| → ∃ e : Point, between a e b ∧ |(a─e)| = |(c₀─c₁)|
nl_statement: For two given unequal straight-lines, to cut off from the greater a straight-line equal to the lesser. Let $AB$ and $C$ be the two given unequal straight-lines, of which let the greater be $AB$.  <prf> So $AE$ is also equal to $C$ [C.N.~1]. Thus, for two given unequal straight-lines, $AB$ and $C$, the (straight-line) $AE$, equal to the lesser $C$, has been cut off from the greater $AB$.
